_notes: T2.108 -- the G-C measurement corpus. Content first, origins second.
Every entry is a capture that a working agent could plausibly have made,
and the corroboration structure is a property of WHO captured WHAT and
WHEN, never of a per-memory unique origin_key. Echo is not evidence: the
`echo` group below states one claim three times from ONE capture session
and is expected never to promote, and the `under-sourced` group states one
claim from two same-week sessions of the same kind, which is k=2 against
N=3. Both are results, not defects.
Four groups, three of which target a different threshold gate:
diversity  -- project `default`. A payments service whose dependency set
is recorded in memory by the agents working on it AND
independently asserted by the indexed repository's own
parsed imports (repo_fixture.json). Two attributable
origins of two kinds (`memory`, `code`) is the diversity
gate, N=2. This is doc 10 6's designed bridge, not a
contrivance: the parse and the human note are genuinely
independent witnesses of the same dependency.
time_gap   -- project `atlas`. A data platform whose operational facts
were recorded once in April and independently re-recorded
by a DIFFERENT session in May, during an incident review.
Two attributable origins >= 7 days apart is N=2.
none       -- project `ledger`. An incident week in which three separate
agent sessions each recorded the same platform facts within
three days. No gate fires (same kind, gap < 7 days), so the
default N=3 applies and three origins meet it exactly.
controls   -- project `ledger`. The two shapes that must NOT promote.
Session identity is `origin_key`, spelled the way the capture doors spell
it (`app.api.mcp.client_identity.resolve_origin_key`): `<source>:<id>`,
where the id is a per-process-boot agent-run id, so one agent run is one
origin however many memories it saves.
TWO EDITING CONSTRAINTS, both machine-checked -- read them before adding
or renaming an entry:
1. `key` carries the claim grouping. A trailing SINGLE-character
segment is a variant marker (`at-k8s-a`/`-b`, `ld-postgres-1`..`-3`)
and everything before it is the claim; any other key is its own
claim. So a key ending in `-c` or `-2` groups with its siblings, and
a lone one is refused by validate_claim_key_convention rather than
inventing a claim nobody wrote down. Give a standalone entry a final
segment of two characters or more.
2. Every `diversity` claim depends on repo_fixture.json ACROSS FILES:
its second origin is the repository's parsed import of the same
package, so a claim whose dependency is missing from that file's
`imports` would still load and run and would silently hold at one
origin. validate_diversity_group_against_fixture refuses it -- add
the import edge in the same edit as the claim.
`memory_id` is NOT stored here: the loader derives it as uuid5 of `key`
under a fixed namespace, so the corpus is reproducible by construction and
an id cannot be hand-edited into a collision.
`created_at` is the capture time and it is load-bearing -- it is what the
time-gap gate is defined over (doc 08 4.1, 'assertions >= 7 days apart
across distinct sessions'). See promotion_corpus.simulate_capture_time_
provenance for how that declared timeline reaches fact_sources, and the
T2.108 report for why that step is disclosed as simulation.

payments-gateway depends on boto3 to write settlement files to object storage.

payments-gateway depends on alembic for its schema migrations.
payments-gateway depends on prometheus_client to export its latency histograms.
